body.statement: For every fixed \(K\) and \(b\), every rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary entries and menus constant in \(a\), every rational contrast \(c\), and every size profile \(s\), does the handle \(\mathfrak C\) admit a complete Turing-model proof that constructs the exact rational orbit kernel, weakly optimizes \(\mathsf P\) and \(\mathsf Q\), and returns in time polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size, the rational input bit length, and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) a rational design, endpoint estimator table, and least-favorable prior with directly checkable bounds \(\underline R\le R^\star\le\overline R\) and \(\overline R-\underline R\le\varepsilon\), together with a total continuous-outcome decoder on every zero-probability face?
body.justification: The general finite conic game is not yet implementable until coefficient growth, weak optimization, outward rounding, and zero-face decoding are controlled in bits even for boundary or label-constant menus.
body.gap: Kallus2021 establishes mixed-strategy optimality without a bit-certified exact orbit compiler, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 gives a polynomial approximation for a different graph design while conjecturing hardness of its full game.
body.consumer: An experimental team can archive a machine-checkable risk interval and a deployable randomization-and-analysis protocol instead of an unaudited floating-point optimum.
